events.text:
Yes. I think this can become one of the **most interesting parts of the capstone**, because it closes a gap that already exists in `project-context`.

Your existing `F4-externalise-admit-recall.md` already asks whether information can leave live context and later return at the right moment, including an arm for **agent-authored state with status and provenance**. Then `F10-compiler-integration.md` is explicitly supposed to test whether all the mechanisms work together.

I would turn the CogExt idea into a new component between those two:

# **Context Runtime**

### A self-maintaining context system for long-running agents

Inside it, the main new subsystem would be the **Context Ledger**.

```text
                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │ OpenCode interaction│
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
                      observe messages,
                    tool results, decisions
                               │
                               ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │   Context Ledger    │
                    │                     │
                    │ obligations         │
                    │ decisions           │
                    │ assumptions         │
                    │ failures            │
                    │ constraints         │
                    │ pending evidence    │
                    │ dependencies        │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
                       lifecycle + scope
                               │
                               ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │ Context Activator   │
                    │ "What matters now?" │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
                     ContextCandidate[]
                               │
                               ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │ Context Compiler    │
                    │ existing Stage 3   │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
                    selected + ordered +
                    represented + budgeted
                               │
                               ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │ OpenCode injection  │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
                            Model
                               │
                         tool results
                               │
                               └──────────────► Ledger
```

That is considerably more powerful than simply remembering commitments.

## What the Ledger would remember

The important move is to generalise CogExt's "promise" into a **typed piece of future-relevant state**.

| Kind                   | Example                                        | Why it might return                           |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `obligation`           | "Update the docs after the parser tests pass." | Tests later pass                              |
| `constraint`           | "Do not modify the database migration."        | Agent begins working in migration area        |
| `decision`             | "Schema v2 is canonical."                      | Code involving schema is opened               |
| `assumption`           | "The API probably returns null here."          | Relevant, but must retain `unverified` status |
| `unresolved_failure`   | "`test_import_legacy` still fails."            | Related module becomes active                 |
| `dependency`           | "Release requires benchmark completion."       | Release task appears                          |
| `pending_verification` | "Fix seems correct but hasn't been tested."    | Tests/tool become available                   |
| `result`               | "Benchmark X produced artifact Y."             | Result is referenced later                    |

That gives you something richer than conventional memory.

The runtime knows not just:

> "I have seen this before."

It knows:

> **"This is an unresolved constraint, created here, verified to this degree, relevant to these scopes, and it should become model context when these conditions hold."**

That is very much the thesis of your Context book.

---

# The particularly cool part: **activation**

I would make this the novel part of the project.

CogExt basically does:

```text
open commitments
      ↓
put them back into context
```

Your system should do:

```text
all durable state
      ↓
activation conditions
      ↓
eligible state
      ↓
Context Compiler
      ↓
only the useful representation
      ↓
current context
```

An entry might therefore look conceptually like:

```json
{
  "id": "state-081",
  "kind": "obligation",
  "statement": "Update the documentation after parser tests pass.",
  "status": "blocked",
  "authority": "agent-authored",
  "confidence": 0.97,

  "scope": {
    "repo": "project-context",
    "paths": ["src/project_context/parser/**"]
  },

  "activation": {
    "when": "tests:parser == pass"
  },

  "depends_on": ["state-079"],

  "source": {
    "session": "...",
    "invocation": "..."
  }
}
```

Initially it stays **outside context**.

Then the tests pass:

```text
pytest parser
      ↓
verification event
      ↓
state-079 = satisfied
      ↓
state-081 becomes actionable
```

The next appropriate request gets:

```text
[ACTIVE PROJECT STATE]

Obligation:
Documentation should be updated now that the parser tests have passed.

Source: prior agent decision
Status: actionable
Scope: parser subsystem
```

And if the user instead asks about CSS, it never enters the window.

That distinction is huge.

**Persistence does not imply admission.**

---

# It also gives you a beautiful contradiction mechanism

This is the CogExt idea I'd definitely adopt.

Imagine the ledger contains:

```text
decision-14
Schema v1 remains canonical.
status = active
```

Later:

```text
decision-31
Schema v2 replaces schema v1.
```

Do **not** simply store both and retrieve them based on similarity.

Instead:

```text
decision-14 ──superseded-by──► decision-31
```

Now the compiler can see:

```text
decision-14
status = superseded
DO NOT ADMIT
```

while:

```text
decision-31
status = active
ADMISSION CANDIDATE
```

This directly exercises several things your book already talks about:

**freshness → authority → contradiction → representation → admission → assembly.**

It is much more interesting experimentally than ordinary vector memory.

---

# And verification makes it even better

I'd borrow CogExt's evidence idea but broaden it.

Agent-generated state should **never automatically become authoritative fact**.

Suppose the agent says:

> "I fixed the race condition."

Ledger:

```text
kind: claim
status: pending_verification
authority: agent
```

Then the tool runs:

```text
pytest tests/test_race.py
```

and it fails.

Now:

```text
claim
  ↓ contradicted_by
test result
```

The next context should not say:

> Race condition fixed.

It could instead say:

```text
UNRESOLVED FAILURE

A previous agent claimed the race condition was fixed,
but subsequent verification failed.

Evidence:
pytest tests/test_race.py → FAIL
```

That is **much more valuable than memory**.

It is context with provenance and epistemic state.

---

# This fits your existing architecture extremely cleanly

I would **not modify the existing read-only OpenCode capture plugin**. Your `AGENTS.md` explicitly pins the invariant that it never mutates context.

Keep that invariant.

Add a second integration:

```text
integrations/
    opencode/                 ← existing observer; remains sacred/read-only

    opencode-runtime/         ← NEW, explicitly intervention-capable
```

And add something approximately like:

```text
src/project_context/
    ledger/
        records.py
        events.py
        lifecycle.py
        store.py
        verification.py
        contradiction.py

    activation/
        request.py
        rules.py
        scorer.py
        trace.py

    runtime/
        assemble.py
        receipt.py
        service.py
```

The existing compiler then remains the compiler.

The new system merely produces candidates for it.

```text
ContextLedger
       │
       ├── active constraint
       ├── relevant decision
       ├── unresolved failure
       └── pending obligation
                 │
                 ▼
        ContextCandidate[]
                 │
                 ▼
         EXISTING COMPILER
```

That separation is important.

The ledger determines **what could matter**.

The activator determines **what might matter now**.

The compiler determines **what gets into the finite window**.

The model determines **what to do with it**.

Those are four different problems.

---

# The capstone demo could be fantastic

Imagine recording a 30–50 step coding project.

Early in the trajectory the agent learns:

```text
Schema v2 is required.

Do not modify migration 017.

There is an unresolved Windows path bug.

After compatibility tests pass,
remove the old adapter.

The benchmark result has not been verified.

The README still describes the previous API.
```

Then you deliberately move through several tasks and sessions.

Twenty calls later the user says:

> Finish the compatibility work.

Instead of giving the model the previous 100,000 tokens of conversation, the runtime reconstructs something like:

```text
ACTIVE CONTEXT STATE

[REQUIREMENT]
Schema v2 is canonical.
verified: user instruction

[CONSTRAINT]
Migration 017 must not be modified.
authority: user

[UNRESOLVED FAILURE]
Windows path handling remains failing.
evidence: test_windows_paths.py

[BLOCKED OBLIGATION]
Remove the old adapter after compatibility tests pass.

[STALE / OMITTED]
Benchmark assumption from session 4.
reason: superseded

[IRRELEVANT / OMITTED]
Documentation task concerning unrelated telemetry.
```

Then your existing Context Compiler decides what fits.

And the Context Debugger could explain:

```text
Ledger candidates:       37
Activated:                 8
Eligibility rejected:      4
Compiler candidates:       4
Admitted:                   3
Token cost:               214

Why was migration-017 included?
  authority=user
  scope=compatibility
  active=true
  constraint=true
  dependency distance=1

Why wasn't README work included?
  scope mismatch
```

**That is a real product**, not merely a book demonstration.

---

# It also gives you an excellent experiment

Your existing F4 design is already almost ready for it. I would add an **F4B — Stateful Context Ledger** before F10.

The matched conditions could be:

| Condition             | Behaviour                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| **C0 No state**       | Previous information disappears            |
| **C1 Full history**   | Keep historical material resident          |
| **C2 All-active**     | CogExt-style: inject every unresolved item |
| **C3 Relevant state** | Activate by current task                   |
| **C4 Compiler state** | Activation + existing Context Compiler     |
| **C5 Oracle**         | Exact state required for the task          |

And importantly, seed the trajectories with **useful state, irrelevant state, stale state, contradictory state, premature claims and conditional obligations**.

Then measure the things your new experiment contract already supports:

```text
task success
false admission
missed required state
stale-state use
contradiction use
requirement survival
token consumption
extra retrieval calls
harmful action
decision-trace completeness
```

My strongest expectation isn't necessarily that `C4` wins every task. The interesting empirical question is whether:

```text
ALL UNRESOLVED STATE
```

is measurably worse than:

```text
THE RIGHT UNRESOLVED STATE
```

That is a **perfect Context From First Principles question**.

---

# Then F10 becomes the real capstone

Right now F10 says:

> Core compiler + surviving passes.

After this work, the full system becomes:

```text
Observe
   ↓
Externalise
   ↓
Maintain typed state
   ↓
Verify / supersede / expire
   ↓
Recall / activate
   ↓
Govern
   ↓
Choose representation
   ↓
Compile
   ↓
Inject
   ↓
Observe outcome
   ↓
Update state
```

And that is the big idea I would build toward:

> **An AI should not carry its whole past forward. It should maintain an external model of potentially useful state and reconstruct the context required for the next computation.**

CogExt gives us a really good concrete mechanism for one slice of that problem — lifecycle-managed commitments. `project-context` can generalise it into a **context runtime**.

I think **Context Runtime + Context Ledger** is strong enough to become the practical capstone product of the book, with the existing Context Debugger as the observational half and the existing Context Compiler as the decision-making half. It would make the repository feel like all the individual chapters eventually converge into one working machine.-----  This first prompt makes the local agent **earn the mechanism before wiring it into live context**. The deliverable is a deterministic, append-only **Context Ledger** with typed state, lifecycle, provenance, contradiction/supersession relationships, fixtures, CLI inspection, and tests. No LLM extraction, retrieval, activation, or injection yet.

# Implement Stage 6A — Context Ledger Foundation

You are working in:

`https://github.com/ernanhughes/project-context`

This repository is the executable experimental companion to the book **Context From First Principles — Engineering What an AI Gets to Know**.

Before changing anything, read and obey:

* `AGENTS.md`
* `README.md`
* `specs/architecture.md`
* `specs/evidence-model.md`
* `specs/experiment-contract.md`
* `specs/measurement-contract.md`
* `specs/failure-taxonomy.md`
* `specs/privacy.md`
* `experiments/designs/F4-externalise-admit-recall.md`
* `experiments/designs/F10-compiler-integration.md`

Also inspect the existing implementations under:

* `src/project_context/domain/`
* `src/project_context/compiler/`
* `src/project_context/debugger/`
* `src/project_context/runs/`
* `src/project_context/cli/`
* `integrations/opencode/`
* relevant tests and fixture conventions.

Do not assume the repository still matches any description in this prompt. **The repository is authoritative.**

---

# Goal

Build the first foundation of a new stateful runtime for Context Lab:

## Context Ledger

The Context Ledger represents durable pieces of potentially future-relevant state produced during AI work.

Examples include:

* obligations;
* constraints;
* decisions;
* assumptions;
* unresolved failures;
* dependencies;
* pending verification;
* verified results.

The important distinction is:

> Persisted state is not automatically context.

Stage 6A implements only the persistent state and lifecycle substrate.

Later stages will decide:

1. whether a ledger item is relevant to a future computation;
2. whether it is eligible for admission;
3. how it should be represented;
4. whether the Context Compiler admits it under budget;
5. where it should be positioned;
6. whether it should actually be injected into a live model request.

**Do not implement those later decisions now.**

The architecture we are moving toward is:

```text
interaction / tools / agent output
              │
              ▼
       Context Ledger
              │
    typed durable state
              │
              ▼
      Context Activator       ← later stage
              │
      ContextCandidate[]
              │
              ▼
      Context Compiler        ← already exists
              │
              ▼
       Runtime Injection      ← later stage
              │
              ▼
            Model
```

Stage 6A owns only:

```text
events
   ↓
typed ledger state
   ↓
lifecycle transitions
   ↓
provenance
   ↓
relationships
   ↓
deterministic inspection
```

---

# Why this belongs in this repository

Do not create a generic memory framework.

The mechanism is specifically intended to support the questions already raised by the Context book and the existing F4 experiment:

```text
externalisation
admission
recall
self-generated state
memory as a source
freshness
authority
contradiction
assembly
```

F4 already separates:

```text
externalisation → admission → recall
```

Stage 6A introduces the state substrate required to make the self-generated-state arm rigorous.

F10 will eventually test whether this state mechanism composes successfully with the rest of the Context Compiler.

---

# Third-party inspiration boundary

We studied CogExt conceptually.

Useful ideas include:

* commitments becoming first-class structured records;
* lifecycle status rather than unstructured text;
* contradiction/supersession relationships;
* verification changing state;
* append-only state history;
* future reinsertion of unresolved information.

Do **not** copy CogExt source code.

Do not reproduce its architecture mechanically.

The Context Ledger is broader and has a different purpose:

> CogExt primarily asks whether commitments remain unresolved.

The Context Ledger asks:

> What potentially future-relevant state exists, what is its epistemic/lifecycle status, and is it still a valid candidate for some future computation?

Implement independently using the conventions already established in `project-context`.

---

# Process requirement: design before implementation

`AGENTS.md` says mechanisms must be earned by experiment/design evidence.

Before implementing production code, inspect whether the repository already contains an appropriate Stage 6/F4B design or preregistration.

If it does, use it.

If it does not, create:

`experiments/designs/F4B-stateful-context-ledger.md`

This is a **design**, not a fabricated experiment and not a frozen result.

The design should state:

## Question

Can agent- or tool-produced information be externalised as typed durable state while retaining enough provenance, lifecycle, authority and verification information for later admission decisions?

## Scope

Stage 6A tests state representation and lifecycle mechanics only.

It does **not** claim that the ledger improves model behaviour.

## Future experimental comparison

Record the intended later matched conditions, but do not execute them yet:

```text
C0 no persisted state
C1 full historical context
C2 all unresolved state
C3 task-activated state
C4 activated + Context Compiler
C5 oracle required state
```

Future trajectories should eventually contain:

* useful active state;
* irrelevant active state;
* stale state;
* superseded state;
* contradictory state;
* unverified claims;
* failed verification;
* conditional obligations;
* resolved obligations;
* scope mismatches.

Make explicit that Stage 6A does not test these behavioural outcomes yet.

---

# Core design principle

The ledger must distinguish at least four separate concepts:

```text
observation
    what happened

state
    what durable proposition/obligation/etc. currently exists

event
    what changed that state

context admission
    whether this state is shown to a model
```

Stage 6A implements the first three.

It must **not** conflate the existence of state with admission to context.

---

# Proposed package

Prefer a new package:

```text
src/project_context/ledger/
```

Likely files:

```text
src/project_context/ledger/
    __init__.py
    records.py
    events.py
    lifecycle.py
    relationships.py
    store.py
    projection.py
```

These names are guidance, not mandatory.

Adapt them to the repository's established style if a better fit exists.

Do not put experiment-specific logic directly into reusable production modules unless the repo's existing promotion rules justify it.

---

# Primary record: LedgerItem

Create an immutable/versioned record representing one durable state item.

Use repository conventions for:

* dataclasses/Pydantic/plain classes;
* schema versions;
* JSON serialization;
* IDs;
* hashing;
* timestamps;
* validation.

Do not introduce a new framework.

A ledger item should conceptually support:

```text
id
schema_version

kind
statement

status

authority
confidence / epistemic status

scope

source provenance

created_at
updated_at or projected_at

activation metadata placeholder if justified
verification metadata

relationships

content identity / semantic identity where appropriate
```

But do not blindly implement every field above.

First determine which belong:

* directly on the item;
* on events;
* on relationships;
* in future stages.

Keep the Stage 6A schema minimal but sufficient.

---

# Item kinds

Support a controlled vocabulary.

Initial kinds should cover approximately:

```text
obligation
constraint
decision
assumption
unresolved_failure
dependency
pending_verification
result
```

If repository terminology suggests a better decomposition, document the change.

Do not permit arbitrary free-form kinds if existing project conventions favour enums.

Each kind should have explicit semantics.

Examples:

### obligation

Something expected to happen later.

```text
Update the documentation once parser compatibility tests pass.
```

### constraint

Something that restricts future actions.

```text
Migration 017 must not be modified.
```

### decision

A choice currently treated as operative.

```text
Schema v2 is canonical.
```

### assumption

A proposition being used without sufficient verification.

```text
The provider probably returns null for this case.
```

### unresolved_failure

A known failure that remains active.

```text
Windows path normalization test still fails.
```

### dependency

A relationship in which some state/action depends on another condition.

```text
Release depends on compatibility benchmark completion.
```

### pending_verification

A claim that should not yet be promoted to verified truth.

```text
The race condition appears fixed, but tests have not run.
```

### result

An evidence-backed result or outcome.

```text
Compatibility suite passed at commit abc123.
```

---

# Authority and epistemic state

Do not make all remembered statements equivalent.

A ledger entry must be capable of preserving distinctions such as:

```text
user instruction
tool observation
repository fact
agent-authored statement
derived state
```

Inspect the existing authority concepts in the compiler before inventing another incompatible vocabulary.

Reuse or map cleanly where possible.

Similarly distinguish epistemic states such as:

```text
asserted
unverified
verified
contradicted
```

Do not overload lifecycle status with epistemic status if they represent different dimensions.

For example:

```text
kind = obligation
lifecycle = active
verification = unverified
```

may be meaningful.

Use the smallest model that preserves these distinctions correctly.

---

# Lifecycle

Implement an explicit deterministic lifecycle.

Do not allow arbitrary string assignment to status.

Possible states might include:

```text
active
blocked
satisfied
failed
superseded
cancelled
expired
contradicted
```

The exact vocabulary should be decided after examining existing repository terminology.

Transitions must be explicit.

For example:

```text
active → blocked
blocked → active

active → satisfied
active → failed
active → superseded
active → cancelled
active → expired
active → contradicted
```

Terminal states should generally not silently return to active.

If reopening is required, model it explicitly as a new item/event rather than mutating historical truth.

Invalid transitions must fail loudly.

---

# Append-only event model

This is essential.

Do not persist state merely by overwriting the current record.

Every meaningful change must be represented by an append-only event.

For example:

```text
LedgerItemCreated
LedgerItemBlocked
LedgerItemUnblocked
LedgerItemVerified
LedgerItemContradicted
LedgerItemSatisfied
LedgerItemFailed
LedgerItemSuperseded
LedgerItemCancelled
LedgerItemExpired
RelationshipAdded
```

Again, use naming consistent with the repo.

An event should preserve enough information to answer:

```text
what changed?
which item?
when?
why?
because of what source/evidence?
from what previous state?
to what next state?
```

Current state should be a **projection of events**, not the authoritative mutable history.

A replay from the event stream must deterministically reconstruct the same ledger state.

Add a test proving this.

---

# Relationships

Support explicit typed relationships between ledger items.

At minimum consider:

```text
depends_on
blocks
supersedes
contradicts
verifies
derived_from
```

Do not flatten these into prose.

Relationships must reference stable IDs.

Examples:

```text
decision-031 --supersedes--> decision-014
```

```text
test-result-882 --contradicts--> claim-441
```

```text
obligation-091 --depends_on--> verification-033
```

Directional semantics must be documented.

Prevent impossible references if practical.

Do not automatically infer semantic contradictions in Stage 6A.

The fixture/test harness may explicitly provide relationships.

Semantic detection comes later.

---

# Verification model

Stage 6A should support **recording verification**, not performing arbitrary verification.

For example, a tool result may eventually produce:

```text
claim:
    "The race condition is fixed."

status:
    pending_verification
```

Then an explicit deterministic event may record:

```text
verification evidence:
    pytest tests/test_race.py

result:
    failed
```

The projection can then mark the prior claim contradicted or failed according to a declared rule.

Do not add an LLM verifier.

Do not call external services.

Do not inspect arbitrary repositories or execute side-effecting tools as part of ledger projection.

The Stage 6A mechanism consumes already-supplied evidence.

---

# Store

Implement a deliberately boring local append-only store.

Prefer the simplest format consistent with repository architecture.

Likely:

```text
JSONL
```

under a local-only path such as:

```text
.local/ledger/
```

unless existing run/state storage conventions suggest something better.

Requirements:

* append-only;
* deterministic parsing;
* schema validation;
* corruption fails loudly;
* no silent dropping of invalid events;
* no mutation of historic events;
* privacy-safe defaults;
* no committed real user data.

Do not introduce Postgres, SQLite, Redis or another service unless the current repository architecture clearly requires one.

The Context Ledger is an experiment/runtime component, not a SaaS backend.

---

# Deterministic projection

Provide something conceptually like:

```python
project(events) -> LedgerState
```

The same ordered event sequence must always yield the same state.

No:

* network;
* model;
* clock dependence inside projection;
* randomness;
* filesystem scanning;
* hidden global state.

If timestamps matter, they must come from recorded events, not `now()` during replay.

Projection should retain:

```text
current items
current lifecycle states
relationships
verification state
provenance
event lineage
```

---

# Identity

Follow existing project identity rules.

Do not invent IDs from secret/private content.

If fixture identities are deterministic, use fixture-stable IDs.

If live identities are UUIDs, preserve that convention.

Consider whether the ledger needs both:

```text
item identity
semantic identity
```

because two records may represent successive versions of the same underlying proposition.

Do not add this merely because it sounds useful; inspect existing `ContextItem` identity semantics first.

---

# Scope

Ledger state needs enough scope information for future activation.

Stage 6A should **record scope**, but not use it to retrieve/activate items yet.

Possible scope dimensions:

```text
repository
workspace
branch
path
component
task
session
agent
```

Do not require all fields.

Use explicit nullable/optional fields.

Do not infer scope from prose.

Fixtures must supply it directly.

Future activation can use it.

---

# Future activation metadata

Do not implement the Context Activator yet.

However, ensure Stage 6A does not make future activation impossible.

A conditional obligation like:

```text
Update docs after parser tests pass.
```

should be representable as:

```text
obligation
    ↓ depends_on
verification/test-state
```

rather than burying the trigger only inside prose.

Prefer relationships and typed metadata over a miniature arbitrary expression language.

Do **not** build a rules engine in Stage 6A.

---

# Compiler boundary

Do not modify the Context Compiler's selection algorithm in this stage.

Do not give ledger items automatic admission privileges.

Do not add ledger-specific exceptions such as:

```python
if candidate.source == "ledger":
    always_include()
```

Later the activator will turn eligible ledger state into ordinary:

```text
ContextCandidate[]
```

and the existing compiler will decide what gets admitted.

The future interface should therefore look conceptually like:

```text
LedgerState
    ↓
Activator
    ↓
ContextCandidate[]
    ↓
existing Context Compiler
```

Stage 6A stops at `LedgerState`.

---

# OpenCode boundary

This is critical.

The existing OpenCode V2 integration is intentionally read-only.

Do not weaken that invariant.

Do not change:

```text
integrations/opencode/
```

into a mutating plugin.

Do not set hook results.

Do not inject text.

Do not rewrite system prompts.

Do not filter tools.

Do not alter messages.

Do not add automatic runtime intervention to the existing capture adapter.

A future stage may create a **separate explicitly intervention-capable integration**, likely something conceptually like:

```text
integrations/opencode-runtime/
```

That is **not Stage 6A**.

Existing capture must remain independently useful and provably read-only.

---

# No automatic extraction yet

Do not build:

```text
LLM output
    ↓
automatic obligation extraction
```

yet.

Stage 6A should ingest explicit structured fixture/events.

Automatic extraction introduces a different experimental question:

```text
Can a model reliably identify state worth persisting?
```

1: # Context From First Principles — book architecture
2: 
3: ## Core definition
4: 
5: **Context is the information made available to a model for a particular computation.**
6: 
7: Keep these terms separate:
8: 
9: - **Available information**: everything the surrounding system could potentially access.
10: - **Session state**: information persisted across turns or actions, whether or not it is currently shown to the model.
11: - **Context**: the information represented in the current model invocation and able to influence this computation.
12: - **Context window**: the model/runtime capacity that bounds the invocation.
13: - **Context engineering**: deliberate selection, representation, arrangement, preservation, transformation, externalization, recovery, and removal of information for a model computation.
14: 
15: The durable first-principles decomposition is:
16: 
17: ```text
18:                  CONTEXT
19:                     │
20:         ┌───────────┼───────────┐
21:         ↓           ↓           ↓
22:     CAPACITY      CONTENT    REPRESENTATION
23:     how much?     which bits?  represented how?
24:                     │
25:                     ↓
26:                   TIME
27:          how does the bundle change?
28: ```
29: 
30: ## Seven-question spine
31: 
32: 1. **What information could the system make available?**
33: 2. **What should the model see for this task now?**
34: 3. **In what representation and order should it see it?**
35: 4. **What must remain exact, and what may lose fidelity?**
36: 5. **What can leave the window, and can it be recovered when needed?**
37: 6. **How should context change as the session and world change?**
38: 7. **Did this context improve behaviour enough to justify its cost?**
39: 
40: ## Method
41: 
42: ```text
43: real task / trace
44:       ↓
45: observe the rendered context
46:       ↓
47: baseline
48:       ↓
49: measured or reproducible failure
50:       ↓
51: smallest intervention
52:       ↓
53: controlled comparison
54:       ↓
55: remove / restore or other ablation
56:       ↓
57: real OpenCode validation
58:       ↓
59: keep, revise, or delete the mechanism
60: ```
61: 
62: A fluent summary is not evidence that compaction worked. A smaller prompt is not evidence that cost fell. A retrieved document is not evidence that it helped. Behaviour, information survival, cache economics, latency, and cost must be measured separately.
63: 
64: ## Book boundary
65: 
66: ```text
67: Retrieval  → generates context candidates
68: Memory     → supplies durable context candidates
69: Tools      → describe capabilities and produce observations
70: Agents     → repeatedly consume and create context
71: MCP       → transports potential context/capabilities
72: Models     → compute over context
73: Context    → decides what is represented for this computation
74: ```
75: 
76: Retrieval, Memory, Agents, Embeddings, Evaluation, Tool Use, and Inference should be referenced only where their boundary with context is necessary.
77: 
78: ## Parts
79: 
80: ### Part I — See the thing
81: 1. What Context Means
82: 2. The Measurement Instrument
83: 3. The Context You Didn't Type
84: 4. The Context Window Is a Budget
85: 5. More Is Not Better
86: 6. Order Changes Meaning
87: 7. Not All Tokens Are Equal
88: 
89: ### Part II — Capacity and reduction
90: 8. Make the Window Bigger
91: 9. Reuse Before Recompute
92: 10. Remove What No Longer Matters
93: 11. Compression Is Loss
94: 12. Let Old Context Fade
95: 
96: ### Part III — Context outside and around the window
97: 13. Externalize the Working Set
98: 14. Bring Back Only What You Need
99: 15. The Agent Writes Its Own Context
100: 16. Memory Is a Context Source
101: 17. Tools Produce Context
102: 18. Representation Is Part of Context
103: 
104: ### Part IV — Govern, assemble, prove
105: 19. Who Gets to Be Right?
106: 20. Context Goes Stale
107: 21. Keep Context in the Right World
108: 22. Assemble for the Task
109: 23. Did the Context Help?
110: 24. The Context Compiler
111: 
112: ## Provider/repository case-study policy
113: 
114: OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, OpenCode, DCP, Magic Context, and WithContext are evidence sources, not the table of contents.
115: 
116: - Claude/Claude Code anchors Chapter 3 because its published/extractable context layers make hidden context inspectable.
117: - DeepSeek, Kimi, and Qwen anchor Chapter 8 because their public architecture makes model-level long-context mechanisms inspectable.
118: - OpenAI and DeepSeek caching anchor Chapter 9.
119: - DCP anchors Chapter 10.
120: - OpenAI/Anthropic compaction plus 2026 compaction research anchor Chapter 11.
121: - Magic Context anchors Chapter 12.
122: - WithContext anchors Chapter 13.
123: 
124: Never infer unpublished internal architecture for closed models.
125: 
126: ## Capstone progression
127: 
128: The working capstone name is **Context Lab**. It is expected to become an OpenCode-oriented context instrument/runtime, but implementation lives outside this book repository.
129: 
130: ```text
131: v0 observe
132: v1 measure
133: v2 deduplicate
134: v3 prune
135: v4 classify/protect
136: v5 compress
137: v6 progressive fidelity
138: v7 externalize
139: v8 recall
140: v9 cache-aware mutation
141: v10 budget + assemble
142:         ↓
143:    CONTEXT COMPILER
144: ```
145: 
146: This ladder is a hypothesis. A stage survives only when experiments earn it.
147: 
148: ## Final architecture as supported by the frozen runs (supersedes the ladder reading)
149: 
150: The frozen runs exercise only the assembly end of the ladder. They neither
151: sustain nor refute pruning, compaction, fidelity, externalisation, recall or
152: cache-aware rewriting, none of which they test; they do not support reading
153: the ladder as sequential maturity stages.
154: `compiler-v1/run-001` (ec642dc) earned construction legality for the
155: staged design over simpler packers; `compiler-behavior-v1/run-003`
156: (ea95e78) showed the extra staged machinery over hard-gated greedy
157: changing no decided action and no score on the matched six-task set,
158: while the hidden-evidence oracle likewise matched staged behaviour
159: exactly. The supported reading, recorded in Chapter 24, is therefore:
160: 
161: ```text
162: small deterministic compiler core
163: (survives: identity/provenance, hard gates, requirements,
164: budget, deterministic assembly/order/render/validate,
165: failure, trace)
166:         +
167: conditional passes, each with a stated tripwire
168: (pruning, compaction, fidelity, externalisation,
169: recall, cache-aware rewrite, representation choice,
170: coverage optimisation)
171:         +
172: behavioural evaluation loop outside the pure function
173: (compile → invoke → observe → evaluate → versioned revision)
174: ```
175: 
176: The ladder above remains the historical hypothesis. Mechanism chapters
177: are not deleted and no experiment is re-scored; the final architecture
178: simply does not present them as earned rungs. A conditional pass
179: activates only when its measured failure exists and its own experiment
180: earns it — the per-pass tripwires are stated in Chapter 24.

1: # Experiment programme
2: 
3: The smallest set of experiments that can support, weaken, merge or reject the
4: book's main mechanisms. Status: **design frozen for review, nothing run.**
5: 
6: The unit of experiment is not the chapter. It is a reusable empirical question that
7: can support several chapters, or a chapter that loses its experiment and is
8: narrowed instead.
9: 
10: ## The empirical story
11: 
12: ```text
13: observe real sessions  →  extract the failure shapes that occur
14:         →  recreate them under control  →  intervene  →  integrate
15: ```
16: 
17: Real traces tell us which failures are worth studying. Controlled fixtures tell us
18: what caused them. This replaces "one chapter, one synthetic demo".

# AGENTS.md — project-context

Instructions for coding agents working in this repository. The companion
book repository (`ernanhughes/context`) owns exposition; this repository
owns executable evidence. Never confuse the two.

## Standing rules

1. **Observation before intervention.** Context Lab v0 observes without
   changing invocations. Add a mechanism only when a frozen book
   experiment has earned it. Proposed stages live in `README.md` and
   `specs/architecture.md`; do not jump ahead.
2. **Never fabricate results.** No invented benchmark numbers, run
   outputs, or telemetry. Synthetic fixtures are labelled `synthetic`
   at creation, in CLI output, and in artifacts. Synthetic is never book
   evidence, no matter how realistic.
3. **Provenance always.** Every number carries its source
   (`provider`, `local-tokenizer`, `approximation`, `unavailable`).
   Unavailable stays `None`, never zero. Costs reference an explicit
   `PriceSchedule` version. Runs reference experiment version, fixture
   version, seed, and git commit.
4. **Hidden truth stays hidden.** Fixture probes, oracle labels, and
   evaluator mappings must never render into model-visible context.
   Add or keep a test pinning this for every fixture.
5. **Private corpus data stays local.** Never commit raw traces,
   credentials, private code, prompts, or personal data. Publication
   requires sanitisation plus recorded human approval
   (`specs/privacy.md`). When in doubt, keep it in `.local/`.
6. **Deterministic fixtures before real traces.** Causal claims come
   from fixtures with ground truth; real traces establish ecological
   relevance only. Never treat a real trace as labelled ground truth.
7. **Independent mechanisms, no copying.** Study third-party
   implementations (notably DCP, AGPL-3.0-or-later) without importing
   their code. Record licences when studying behaviour. Keep this
   repository Apache-2.0-clean: no AGPL source, no vendored snippets.
8. **Small diffs, boring code.** Prefer stdlib and explicit schemas over
   frameworks. Experiment-specific code lives under `experiments/`;
   promote to `src/` only after an experiment justifies it.
9. **Append-only evidence.** Never mutate a recorded observation,
   manifest, or artifact in place. New analysis creates new records
   pointing back at sources.
10. **Validate before claiming.** New records need schema versions and
    round-trip tests. New runs need manifests. New claims need frozen
    artifacts that pass `validate_artifact`.

## Hard process-safety invariant

The experimental tooling observes files generated by OpenCode. It must
never start, stop, kill, restart, or otherwise manage the user's
OpenCode processes: no `taskkill`/`pkill`/`killall`, no process-stop
APIs, no search-and-kill by process name, no TUI lifecycle management,
no ownership claims over pre-existing sessions. Capture is user-driven;
analysis reads files. A source scan test pins this invariant.

## Stage 3 compiler invariants

19. **Hard illegality cannot be laundered through relevance.** A
    scope/freshness/authority/floor rejection is terminal; no score,
    rank, or weight revives the candidate.
20. **No silent mandatory truncation.** Minimum legal content that does
    not fit is `CompileFailure`, never a shortened bundle.
21. **No final-render slicing.** Overruns repair by policy-governed
    removal and rerender, or fail.
22. **Hidden oracle truth never enters compiler runtime.** Truth files,
    evaluator labels, and oracle minima live under evaluation code and
    fixture truth files; production compiler modules must not import
    them. Tests pin the import direction and the absence of oracle
    identifiers in compiler sources.
23. **Compile failure is a valid expected result.** Mandatory overflow,
    missing required sources, and illegal representations must fail
    loudly with reason codes; tests assert exact failures.
24. **Successful bundles must validate.** Rendered cost within budget,
    mandatory presence, floors, closures, and layout invariants hold on
    every emitted bundle.
25. **No model or network calls in compiler-v1.** The suite runs fully
    offline; relevance scores are fixture inputs. A source scan test pins
    the forbidden imports.
26. **Policy revisions require full-suite replay.** New policy versions
    rerun every fixture/strategy/budget; historic runs are never edited.
27. **Synthetic results are not ecological evidence.** Frozen compiler
    runs are PROJECT RESULTs about fixture mechanics, never claims about
    real OpenCode contexts or model behaviour.

## Stage 4 behavioural invariants

28. **Never mutate run-001.** Behavioural conditions re-render frozen
    traces and digest-verify them; failures stop the condition.
29. **Never leak evaluator truth to the reader.** Task files, prompts,
    and payloads carry no hidden labels, minima, or expected actions;
    tests scan for them.
30. **Never tune tasks, graders, budgets, or interventions after model
    output.** Fake reader for development; first genuine call freezes
    the experiment (preregistration commit).
31. **Never silently recompile a frozen condition.** Derived bundles get
    new identities with parent/intervention linkage; MR restores
    byte-identically.
32. **Every model call is isolated.** No conversation reuse, no shared
    sessions, no cross-condition state; case IDs encode
    fixture/budget/condition/reader/repeat.
33. **No LLM judge for primary task score.** Deterministic parser plus
    deterministic grader; malformed output is observed, never repaired.
34. **Provider errors are not task failures.** Retry transport errors
    with bounded backoff; record attempts; never substitute models.
35. **None telemetry is not zero.** Unavailable usage, cost, and cache
    fields stay unavailable with provenance intact.
36. **No real side effects.** Inert synthetic fixtures, deterministic
    simulator grading, dummy sinks only.
37. **Policy changes require new versions plus full replay.** Behavioural
    outcomes never edit compiler policy in place.
38. **Behavioural results do not imply ecological prevalence.** Real
    reader behaviour on synthetic tasks is the entire claim until real
    traces exist.

## Stage 1 capture rules (V2, pinned 2.0.16)

11. **Capture is opt-in and off by default.** Never enable raw recording
    by merely installing the adapter; never manage the user's OpenCode
    processes to test capture.
12. **Never mutate OpenCode context.** Copy and serialise only. The
    no-mutation invariant is test-pinned, not just reviewed. Never set
    `event.result` on compaction; never write to the hook event.
13. **Call it V2 model context**, never the provider wire request. The
    V2 `session.hook("context")` boundary yields the assembled semantic
    request; protocol/provider lowering happens after it. Record the
    limitation instead of inferring it away.
14. **Never infer hidden origins from text.** Vendor, product, and
    project attribution require hook metadata, not prose heuristics.
    Debugger categories are structural (ingester kind), never inferred
    from prose. Unattributable fields stay null.
15. **Unavailable stays unavailable.** No zeros for missing telemetry,
    no estimates labelled observed, no past-computation token fields
    transferred into current invocations, no hard-coded model limits,
    no capacities scraped from model names.
16. **Raw captures stay local and unprinted.** Structural output by
    default; no commits, no casual stdout, no uploads. Content search
    is local-only behind an explicit flag.
17. **Observations are not interventions.** Nothing in the adapter or
    the debugger may transform, prune, compact, rewrite, reorder, or
    optimise; the adapter package must keep zero runtime dependencies
    and the debugger must make zero model calls.
18. **Pin API versions.** Adapter records OpenCode plus plugin-package
    versions per capture; never depend on `latest`. A runtime version
    mismatch fails clearly; there is no V1 fallback and no dual-version
    runtime.

## Reproducibility invariants

39. **Runs that support a published claim record the strongest reader
    identity available, and never invent one.** Every live run carries
    `run_purpose` (`evidence` by default, or `exploratory`) and, in its
    manifest, the model digest when the endpoint exposes it
    (`reader_model_digest`, with its source), else `unavailable`. An
    evidence run whose model is a moving alias (no tag, or `:latest`) is
    refused unless `--allow-moving-model-alias` acknowledges it, and is
    then recorded as non-reproducible from the name. Exploratory runs
    (`--exploratory`) may use any model, are labelled as such, and can
    never be cited as confirmatory evidence. Frozen fixture manifests are
    historical records and are never edited to hide an alias; a rerun is
    a new run.
40. **Every frozen run the book cites has a published copy and a
    committed evidence manifest.** Copies live under `evidence/runs/`
    (byte for byte, synthetic runs only, copied by
    `scripts/publish_evidence_runs.py` behind its sanitisation gate) and
    are pinned in `evidence/manifests/` by digest and by numbers
    recomputed from the artifacts (`scripts/evidence_manifest.py`).
    Publishing a new run needs sanitisation plus recorded human approval
    (rule 5, `specs/privacy.md`). Nothing about this constrains
    exploratory work, which stays local.

## Before implementing any mechanism

Check, in order: the book chapter that earns it, the frozen experiment
spec under `experiments/`, and the stage report in `docs/`. If any link
in that chain is missing, write the spec first.
Now in the implementation repo — reading the specs and existing code before designing.

2: 
3: Stage: observation substrate. No interventions exist.
4: 
5: ## Records
6: 
7: | Record | Module | Meaning |
8: |---|---|---|
9: | `ContextItem` | `domain/items.py` | One identifiable unit of a bundle. Frozen. Later-earned fields (retention_class, recoverability, exactness, freshness, groups) deliberately absent. |
10: | `ContextBundle` | `domain/bundles.py` | One rendered context for one invocation. Immutable, order-preserving, content-hashed. |
11: | `ModelInvocation` | `domain/invocations.py` | Actual execution: provider, model, telemetry, cost. Unavailable stays `None`. |
12: | `EvaluationObservation` | `domain/evaluation.py` | PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE evidence with metric, value, evidence, evaluator. Append-only via `EvaluationLog`. |
13: | `RunManifest` | `domain/runs.py` | Reconstruction identity (timestamp excluded). |
14: | `CorpusManifest` | `corpus/manifest.py` | Describes a real trace without containing it. Publication gated. |
15: | `InterventionProposal` | `domain/interventions.py` | Named future kinds only. No behaviour. |
16: 
17: ## Identity rules
18: 
19: - Live captured records: UUIDs.
20: - Deterministic fixture entities: stable IDs (`rule-001`, bundles named
21:   `<fixture>-<version>`); reconstruction via `content_hash()`.
22: - `id` = representation instance; `semantic_id` = underlying information
23:   (reserved for Chapters 11–12). Neither is ever derived from secret content.

28: Fixture / captured invocation
29:         ↓
30: ContextBundle (frozen, ordered, hashed)
31:         ↓
32: ModelInvocation (telemetry, cost under a recorded schedule)
33:         ↓
34: Observation (append-only log)
35:         ↓
36: Evaluation (probe scoring against hidden truth)

140: OpenCode 2.0.16 (V2 API)
141:   session.hook("context") → one observed primary model request
142:   session.hook("compaction") → same shape, kind=compaction (result never set)
143:   session.hook("generate") → same shape, kind=generate
144:         ↓ local spool (.local/... or $PROJECT_CONTEXT_SPOOL_DIR)
145:   Python ingester (no mutation of raw files)
146:         ↓
147:   ContextBundle (provenance: source_type opencode_capture,
148:     request_kind, sequence_index=invocation_sequence)
149:     + ModelInvocation (usage telemetry unavailable at this boundary: all None)
150:         ↓
151:   Context Debugger (src/project_context/debugger/): inspect, timeline,
152:     query, compare, explain, detect — observations, never interventions
153: ```

155: Boundary, stated once: this is **OpenCode V2 semantic model-request
156: context**, not the byte-for-byte provider HTTP request.
157: Protocol/provider lowering happens after the hook; provider-added
158: material, the wire representation, and cache decisions stay
159: unobserved (reported as such, never zero-filled). Stable prefix is
160: structural evidence only, never a cache claim. Repeated is measurable;
161: redundant is not claimed. Large is measurable; harmful is not claimed.
162: Options are observed overrides, never complete effective provider
163: configuration. Tool-definition exposure is availability, never
164: utility. The debugger makes zero model calls.

1: # Experiment contract
2: 
3: No serious experiment runs before its contract exists. Each experiment
4: directory must define, in writing, before execution:
5: 
6: ```text
7: question
8: hypothesis
9: population (fixtures and/or corpus references)
10: independent variable
11: controlled variables
12: conditions
13: measurements (per measurement-contract.md)
14: success / failure criteria
15: falsification criteria
16: seed and repetition strategy
17: provider / model / version (or synthetic)
18: cost ceiling
19: ```
20: 
21: Then, and only then: results.
22: 
23: ## Method (mirrors the book)
24: 
25: ```text
26: observe → baseline → failure → smallest intervention
27: → controlled comparison → ablation / counterfactual
28: → keep, revise, or remove
29: ```
30: 
31: ## Stage 0 scope
32: 
33: Stage 0 experiments are fixture-inspection and schema-validation runs
34: only. No model is called, no money is spent, no intervention is tested.
35: Intervention experiments (pruning onward) each get their own directory
36: under `experiments/` with a frozen `spec.yaml` before any run.
37: 
38: ## Evidence runs (programme contract)
39: 
40: The rules above apply to any experiment. A run that is meant to support a
41: published claim, an **evidence run**, must also satisfy the contract below. It
42: exists for one purpose: **another person must be able to say exactly what
43: changed between two experimental conditions, and nothing else.**
44: 
45: The contract extends the records that already exist. It adds no parallel
46: framework and no new record type; where a field is not already stored, it is a
47: reserved key in `RunManifest.environment`.
48: 
49: ### Where each required fact lives
50: 
51: | Fact | Where it is recorded | Notes |
52: |---|---|---|
53: | experiment id, version | `RunManifest.experiment_id`, `experiment_version` | exists |
54: | experiment family | environment key `experiment_family` | new key |
55: | run id, time | `RunManifest.run_id`, `timestamp` | evidence runs record real UTC time; the fixed placeholder time used by the first three runs is not allowed |
56: | code revision | `RunManifest.git_commit`; environment `vcs_dirty` | evidence runs require a clean tree |
57: | fixture revision | environment `fixture_revision` (digest of the fixture set); `RunManifest.fixture_id`, `fixture_version` | new key |
58: | configuration revision | environment `configuration_revision` (digest of `spec.yaml`, policy and weight files) | new key |
59: | preregistration | environment `preregistration` = `<path>@<commit>` | new key; required for evidence runs |
60: | model provider and name | `RunManifest.provider`, `RunManifest.model` | for a behavioural run these name the **reader**; the synthetic nature of the fixtures is `evidence_class`, not the provider. (The first runs recorded `synthetic` here; that was ambiguous.) |
61: | model version or digest | environment `reader_model_digest` (+ `reader_model_identity_source`); `ModelInvocation.model_version` | required for a live evidence run; `unavailable` is a failure, not a value |
62: | reader identity and role | environment `reader_model`, `reader` (`primary`, `transfer`, ...) | exists for reader runs |
63: | task id, task population | case id encodes fixture; environment `task_population` (generator name and version, or fixture set) | new key |
64: | context condition | `BehaviorRecord.condition_id` | exists |
65: | bundle id, bundle digest | `ModelInvocation.bundle_id`; `BehaviorRecord.source_bundle_digest` | exists |
66: | trial id, seed | case id encodes repeat; `RunManifest.seed`; environment `decoding_seed` | exists |
67: | measurements, outcome | `EvaluationObservation` (metric, value, verdict, evidence) | metric names follow `measurement-contract.md` |
68: | artifact digests | the evidence manifest (`evidence/manifests/`) | derived, committed |
69: | environment | `RunManifest.environment` | exists |
70: | known limitations | the evidence manifest | derived, committed |
71: | run purpose | environment `run_purpose` = `evidence` or `exploratory` | exploratory runs stay local |
72: 
73: `src/project_context/runs/contract.py` checks a manifest for these keys.
74: Exploratory runs need only the `run_purpose` label.
75: 
76: ### What changed between conditions
77: 
78: Every comparison declares its **factor** and the **control** it is measured
79: against. For each condition the case schedule records the control it differs from
80: and the items it added, removed or transformed (the fields `added_ids`,
81: `removed_ids` and the bundle digest already exist for this). A comparison that
82: changes more than its declared factor, for example a different budget or a
83: different reader alongside a different bundle, is not valid evidence for that
84: factor. This is exactly the fault in the first reader-transfer probe, and the
85: rule exists to make it impossible to repeat quietly.
86: 
87: ### Frozen means frozen
88: 
89: Fixtures, graders, prompts and schedules are versioned and fixed before the first
90: model call. Nothing is tuned after outputs are seen. A pilot that shows the
91: interface is unusable (as happened before the first behavioural run) may amend the
92: interface, as a new version, if there is nothing yet to tune against; the amendment

1: # Evidence model
2: 
3: Four evidence classes. Confusing them is the fastest way to corrupt the
4: book, so the repository enforces the vocabulary in code and artifacts.
5: 
6: ## BACKGROUND RESULT
7: 
8: External literature or provider evidence. Lives in the book's
9: `research/bibliography.yaml`. Never stored as a run artifact here.
10: 
11: ## BOOK HYPOTHESIS
12: 
13: A claim awaiting a project-context experiment. Lives in manuscript prose
14: marked as hypothesis. This repository may hold its fixture and its frozen
15: spec, never its result.
16: 
17: ## PROJECT RESULT
18: 
19: A result produced by a frozen run in this repository. Must reference:
20: 
21: ```text
22: run_id
23: git SHA of this repository at run time
24: experiment id and version
25: artifact paths under runs/
26: ```
27: 
28: ## BOOK RESULT
29: 
30: A project result deliberately imported into the manuscript. The prose
31: describes the finding in plain language; the experiment ID, run ID, and
32: commit SHA are resolvable from the claim through the evidence register
33: (`evidence/README.md`) rather than printed in the text. Nothing else in the
34: manuscript may be called a result.
35: 
36: ## Labelling rule
37: 
38: Every bundle, manifest, artifact, and CLI report carries
39: `evidence_class: synthetic | provider-observed`. Validators reject
40: synthetic artifacts that claim provider evidence. Synthetic data is
41: never book evidence, no matter how realistic it looks.

1: # Measurement contract — Context Lab v0
2: 
3: Every measurement recorded by this repository states, at minimum:
4: 
5: 1. **What was measured**: metric name plus the exact record and field.
6: 2. **How**: instrument or procedure version (evaluator id, e.g.
7:    `project_context.scoring.exact_match.v1`).
8: 3. **Provenance of numbers**: `provider`, `local-tokenizer`,
9:    `approximation`, or `unavailable` — per value, never per report.
10: 4. **What is missing**: unobserved components listed, not zero-filled.
11: 5. **Evidence class**: `synthetic` or `provider-observed`, on the bundle,
12:    the manifest, and the artifact.
13: 
14: ## Rules
15: 
16: - Token estimates from `estimate_tokens` are labelled `approximation` at
17:   creation and must never be stored as provider telemetry.
18: - Cost is always computed from an explicit `PriceSchedule` version recorded
19:   alongside the result. Recompute historical costs only under the schedule
20:   that applied at the time.
21: - Latency, cache reads/writes, and reasoning tokens default to unavailable.
22: - Evaluation verdicts (PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE) require stated evidence; a
23:   verdict without an evidence string is invalid.
24: - No measurement may silently mutate the record it measures. Analysis
25:   layers append; raw observations are never rewritten.
26: 
27: ## Stage 1: OpenCode pre-dispatch partial capture
28: 
29: Observed at the hook (V1 experimental transforms, admission, tool-after):
30: 
31: ```text
32: system structure, message order and parts, tool results with call linkage,
33: session/agent/model identity where the hook carries it, hook-time ordering
34: ```
35: 
36: Exact local measurements (no model, no network):
37: 
38: ```text
39: bytes, characters, item counts, content equality via local fingerprints,
40: structural prefix equality within one session scope
41: ```
42: 
43: Derived or estimated (labelled as such):
44: 
45: ```text
46: local token estimate (approximation), repetition classifications,
47: stable-prefix ratios, growth deltas
48: ```
49: 
50: Unavailable at this boundary unless separately observed (stay None,
51: never zero):
52: 
53: ```text
54: provider cache hits, wire payload bytes, provider-added prompt material,
55: final resolved model defaults, provider usage and cost, response latency
56: ```
57: 
58: Assistant-message token/cost fields visible inside stored history describe
59: past computations, never the current invocation; the ingester does not
60: transfer them into invocation telemetry.
61: ## Stage 5: OpenCode V2 model-context capture
62: 
63: Observed at the session context hook (V2 assembled request, primary
64: agent-loop scope unless a kind filter says otherwise):
65: 
66: ```text
67: assembled system structure, message order and parts, tool definitions
68: (description plus input schema, sorted deterministically), tool results
69: with call linkage, session/agent/model identity, invocation sequence,
70: observed request overrides, declared model limits where the API yields
71: them (else UNAVAILABLE)
72: ```
73: 
74: Exact local measurements (no model, no network):
75: 
76: ```text
77: bytes, characters, item counts, content equality via local fingerprints,
78: structural prefix equality within one session scope, tool-definition
79: counts/bytes/share/stability, per-category composition
80: ```
81: 
82: Derived or estimated (labelled as such):
83: 
84: ```text
85: local token estimate (approximation), repetition classifications,
86: stable-prefix ratios, growth deltas, deterministic doctor observations
87: under debugger-doctor-policy-v1 (magnitude only, never harm/utility)
88: ```
89: 
90: Unavailable at this boundary unless separately observed (stay None or
91: UNAVAILABLE, never zero):
92: 
93: ```text
94: provider cache hits, wire payload bytes, provider-added prompt material,
95: complete effective provider configuration, provider usage and cost,
96: response latency
97: ```
98: 
99: The debugger's request `options` are observed overrides: an empty
100: object means no overrides were observed, never that no model defaults
101: exist. Deleting or omitting an override falls back to configured
102: defaults; the debugger must not present overrides as the resolved
103: configuration.
104: 
105: ## Shared measurement vocabulary
106: 
107: Several chapters proposed overlapping measurements. This section defines each once.
108: Chapters and experiments use these terms and these definitions, and add none
109: without adding it here.
110: 
111: Three rules govern all of them:
112: 
113: - **Dimensions stay separate.** There is no composite "context quality" score. A
114:   later analysis may justify combining dimensions, but only by stating why in its
115:   own preregistration.
116: - **Every value carries its provenance** (`provider`, `local-tokenizer`,
117:   `approximation`, `unavailable`), and `unavailable` is never zero.
118: - **Every rate reports its denominator**, and per-task outcomes are kept beside any
119:   aggregate.
120: 
121: ### Behaviour
122: 
123: Scored by deterministic graders over a parsed, schema-constrained action. No
124: model judges any of these.
125: 
126: | Term | Definition | Existing metric |
127: |---|---|---|
128: | task success | 1 when every graded field of the action equals the fixture's correct value, else 0. Partial credit only where the grader defines an objective per-field score in advance | `*:task_score` |
129: | constraint adherence | fraction of the fixture's declared constraints the action does not violate; the per-constraint booleans are kept | family-specific |
130: | harmful action | the action is in the fixture's forbidden set. Harm is defined by the fixture, never inferred | `*:harmful_action` |
131: | unsupported claim | a value in the action that appears in no admitted item and not in the task text (exact match) | new |
132: | abstention | the action is the fixture's abstain action | action name |
133: | evidence use | the action contains the decisive value, and the decisive item was admitted. It is **not** influence: influence is shown only by a remove-and-restore pair | new |
134: | parse success | the response parsed under the frozen schema. Unparseable output is recorded, never repaired | `*:parse_success` |
135: 
136: ### Context
137: 
138: Computed from the rendered bundle and the decision trace.
139: 
140: | Term | Definition |
141: |---|---|
142: | rendered tokens | tokens in the exact rendered bundle, with provenance |
143: | tokens by source | rendered tokens grouped by source kind and item kind |
144: | duplicate tokens | tokens in an item whose bytes are identical to an earlier item in the same bundle or the previous request |
145: | stable prefix | number of leading items (and tokens) identical to the previous request in the same session |
146: | admitted, dropped, transformed | item ids in each state, from the decision trace |
147: | item fidelity | the representation an item was rendered in: full, dense, compact, anchor, reference |
148: | evidence position | position of the decisive item as a fraction of rendered tokens (0 first, 1 last) |
149: | bundle digest | digest of the exact rendered bytes |
150: 
151: ### Information survival
152: 
153: Measured before behaviour, so that "destroyed" and "not used" can be told apart.
154: 
155: | Term | Definition |
156: |---|---|
157: | exact requirement retained | each fixture requirement that must be exact appears verbatim in the rendered bundle |
158: | semantic requirement retained | the fixture's probe questions about it, answerable only from the bundle, are answered correctly. Deterministic where possible, otherwise a frozen rubric with a blinded evaluator, never the reader being tested |
159: | critical evidence recoverable | its pointer resolves, to the right version, with intact bytes |
160: | provenance retained | the claim is rendered with its source and status attached |
161: | rationale retained | a probe asking why a decision was made is answerable from the bundle |
162: 
163: ### Economics and runtime
164: 
165: | Term | Definition |
166: |---|---|
167: | input, output tokens | as reported by the provider or local server |
168: | cache write, read, miss tokens | as reported by the provider, where exposed |
169: | latency, time to first token | wall-clock, where the interface exposes them |
170: | provider cost | computed from an explicit price schedule version recorded with the result |
171: | local compute | wall-clock seconds and the device class, for local models |
172: | call count | model calls made, including retries |
173: 
174: ### Naming
175: 
176: New metrics use `<family>:<term>` in `EvaluationObservation.metric`, matching the
177: existing `hold_release:task_score` style, where the term is one of the names
178: above.

1: # Failure taxonomy
2: 
3: A failed or degraded case is never reported as just "wrong answer". Every one is
4: attributed to a **primary state** by walking a fixed ladder over facts the run
5: established deterministically. The ladder asks, in order: at which stage did the
6: information stop doing its job?
7: 
8: It is implemented in `src/project_context/domain/failure.py`
9: (`FailureState`, `FailureEvidence`, `attribute`) so the same rule is applied by
10: every family.
11: 
12: ## The nine states
13: 
14: | State | Plain meaning | What must be true |
15: |---|---|---|
16: | `CONTROL_FAILURE` | The experiment itself is invalid. | Conditions were not matched, a bundle digest did not verify, or the grader did not run. The case is excluded from every result and counted. |
17: | `ABSENT` | The information was never admitted. | The required item is not in the admitted set (from the decision trace). |
18: | `LOST` | It was admitted, then destroyed. | A transformation removed or changed what had to survive exactly, or a required fact fails its survival check. |
19: | `STALE` | It was true once and is not now. | The action equals the action a stale item in the bundle implies, and the fixture says that item is out of date. |
20: | `SCOPE_LEAK` | The wrong world influenced behaviour. | The action equals the action an out-of-scope item implies. |
21: | `OVERRIDDEN` | A conflicting or higher-authority item drove the action. | The action equals the action implied by an item the policy says must not govern here. |
22: | `UNRECOVERED` | It survived, but the reader did not find or use it. | The item was admitted and survived, and the action does not contain the decisive value. |
23: | `MISAPPLIED` | It was found and used wrongly. | The action contains the decisive value, and the action is still wrong. |
24: | `INTERFERENCE` | Extra context made viable behaviour worse. | The same reader succeeds with the minimal bundle and fails with this one, and no earlier state explains it. |
25: 
26: ## How attribution works
27: 
28: Attribution walks the ladder in the order above and stops at the first state whose
29: fact is **explicitly** false. A fact the run did not establish never triggers a
30: state: unavailable is not false. So a case that was never admitted is `ABSENT`
31: even if it was also misapplied, because nothing downstream could have rescued it.
32: 
33: The facts are booleans produced by the run's own checks, never by asking the reader:
34: 
35: | Fact | Comes from |
36: |---|---|
37: | control valid | matched conditions; verified bundle digests; the grader ran |
38: | required admitted | the decision trace or bundle membership |
39: | required survived | the survival checks (`specs/measurement-contract.md`) |
40: | source current | the fixture's validity state for each item |
41: | in scope | the fixture's scope binding for each item |
42: | no conflicting influence | the action compared with the actions the trap items imply |
43: | evidence used | the action contains the decisive value |
44: | applied correctly | the grader |
45: | degraded versus baseline | the same reader's outcome with the minimal bundle |
46: 
47: ## Fixture obligations
48: 
49: Deterministic attribution needs the fixture to say more than what is correct:
50: 
51: 1. **Trap items carry the action they would induce.** A stale record, an
52:    out-of-scope note or a conflicting instruction each declares, in the hidden
53:    truth, the action a reader following it would take. `STALE`, `SCOPE_LEAK` and
54:    `OVERRIDDEN` are then decided by comparison, not by judgement.
55: 2. **The decisive value is named.** `UNRECOVERED` and `MISAPPLIED` are decided by
56:    whether the action contains it.
57: 3. **A minimal-bundle control exists** for every task, so `INTERFERENCE` has
58:    something to be measured against.
59: 4. Hidden truth never renders into model-visible text (existing invariant).
60: 
61: ## Secondary states
62: 
63: The primary state is the first the ladder finds. Other states that also apply are
64: recorded as secondary, so a case that was stale *and* misapplied is not flattened.
65: Aggregates report the primary state; the secondary states are for diagnosis.
66: 
67: ## What the taxonomy is not
68: 
69: It is not a scoring rule and not a ranking of mechanisms. It says where a failure
70: came from, so that a null result can be explained (the mechanism was never asked to
71: help: `ABSENT`) and a real failure can be located (the mechanism destroyed the
72: information: `LOST`).
73: 
74: ## Applying it to the first three runs
75: 
76: The first behavioural runs were frozen before this taxonomy. Their cases can be
77: re-labelled by analysis, appending new observations that point back at the frozen
78: records, since their hidden truth exists; nothing in them is edited. That
79: re-labelling is not needed to start the programme.

1: # Privacy boundary
2: 
3: This repository is public. Real agent sessions contain credentials, private
4: code, personal data, and customer information. The boundary is structural,
5: not advisory.
6: 
7: ## Never commit by default
8: 
9: ```text
10: credentials, API keys, tokens, private source code,
11: private repository content, personal data, private prompts,
12: private messages, local filesystem secrets, raw connected-account data
13: ```
14: 
15: ## Local-only locations (git-ignored)
16: 
17: ```text
18: .local/          scratch, downloads, transient analysis
19: raw-corpus/      unprocessed real traces (never committed)
20: private-runs/    runs against private material (never committed)
21: runs/*/          frozen run directories, except runs/README.md
22: ```
23: 
24: Only `runs/README.md` (the convention document) is committed. Run
25: artifacts live in CI-local or explicitly published locations per future
26: policy; Stage 0 commits no run artifacts at all.
27: 
28: ## Publication path
29: 
30: Raw material may enter git only through explicit sanitisation plus human
31: approval, recorded as `CorpusManifest.sanitisation_status =
32: "approved-public"`. `assert_publishable()` refuses everything else, and
33: tests pin that refusal. Sanitised-but-unapproved material is still
34: unpublishable: approval is a human decision, not a script output.
35: 
36: ## Identifier hygiene
37: 
38: Never derive stable IDs from secret or private content. Fixture IDs are
39: authored constants; live capture IDs are random UUIDs.
40: 
41: ## OpenCode capture (Stage 1)
42: 
43: Local raw captures may contain source code, conversation text, tool
44: output, system and project instructions, and any secret the model was
45: genuinely shown. Therefore raw captures are private, git-ignored, never
46: uploaded, never automatically sanitised, and never printed casually
47: (`inspect` defaults to structural output; raw printing requires an
48: explicit local flag). Bundle ids (`opencode-<capture-uuid>`) and
49: filenames (UUIDs, never prompt/project/secret-derived) carry no content.
50: Content fingerprints are local-only and never exported; export relabels
51: session keys to ordinals and the gate refuses content, identifier, hash,
52: and secret markers.
53: ## Context Debugger (Stage 5)
54: 
55: The debugger is a local-only product layer over the same raw captures:
56: it makes zero model calls and modifies no context. Default reports are
57: structural only — no raw content, no raw session identifiers (local
58: ordinals such as `local:1` instead), no hashes. Raw content prints only
59: under an explicit local flag (`--show-content`, `--allow-content-search`
60: for substring search), with a local-only warning on stdout. Debugger
61: JSON is deterministic and versioned for a future local TUI; it carries
62: the same structural-only default. Nothing captured or derived is ever
63: sent to a model or the network by debugger code.
64: 
65: ## Approved publications
66: 
67: Run artifacts are private by default. A run may be published only after the
68: sanitisation gate in `scripts/publish_evidence_runs.py` passes and a human
69: approval is recorded here.
70: 
71: | Run | Approved | Approver | Basis |
72: |---|---|---|---|
73: | `compiler-v1/run-001` | 2026-09-24 | project author | synthetic fixtures; gate passed |
74: | `compiler-behavior-v1/run-003` | 2026-09-24 | project author | synthetic tasks, synthetic responses to them; gate passed |
75: | `compiler-behavior-v1/run-003-transfer` | 2026-09-24 | project author | as above; gate passed |
76: 
77: Published runs are copied byte for byte to `evidence/runs/`. The gate refuses
78: any run that is not `evidence_class: synthetic`, and any file containing a
79: machine path, hostname, address, key-like string, credential assignment or
80: e-mail address. It never edits a file and never overwrites a differing one.
81: 
82: The approval covers these three runs only. Real captured sessions
83: (`raw-corpus/`, OpenCode captures) are unaffected: they stay private, and a
84: sanitised derivative of a real corpus needs its own approval under
85: `CorpusManifest.sanitisation_status`.
